Work list

Shimon residence, Redwood City · 15 jobs · 8 September 2026

Everything we’d like done, in the order that matters to us — the first group first, and the rest as time allows. No need to get through all of it in one visit.

A couple of things worth knowing up front: 4 of the 15 are electrical, and items 9 and 10 run in sequence — the brick pad has to go down before the storage unit can be built on it. If the unit hasn’t arrived by the time you’re here, just do the pad and we’ll sort the rest later.

Start with these

The ones that matter most.

4High

Fix side-gate latch + add locks to both side doors

Exterior / hardware

The side-gate latch hardware is worn/rusty and needs replacing. The replacement latch has already been bought — labour only, no parts needed for the latch itself. Also add lock options to BOTH side doors/gates.

5High

Fix broken wall air vent (register)

HVAC / general

The wall HVAC vent cover/register is detached and hanging off the wall — needs reattaching or replacing.

8High

Add an edge to contain the gravel strip

Landscaping / hardscape

The river-rock strip running along the fence between the house and the public sidewalk has no border, so the stones migrate onto the sidewalk and down the driveway — visible across the concrete in the photo. Wants a proper edge, ideally steel landscape edging set slightly proud of the gravel, along the sidewalk side and around where the strip meets the driveway. Roughly 25–30 ft. Worth also raking the gravel down so it sits below the edge rather than mounded, otherwise it will ride over any border.

9High

Lay bricks to make a flat pad for the storage unit

Landscaping / hardscape

Level the dirt and lay bricks to create a flat, stable base for the outdoor storage unit. The bricks have already been bought, so this can go ahead immediately — it does not wait on anything. Needs to be level: resin boxes flex on uneven ground and the lid stops closing properly.

Then these

Worth doing on the same visit if there's time.

2Medium

Electrical

Install lighting at the front entrance.

3Medium

Backyard and backdoor lighting — inspect existing, install fairy lights

Electrical

Two parts, same job. First, inspect the backdoor lights, both the solar ones and the hanging ones. Second, run and install fairy lights across the backyard. Note: the fairy lights themselves haven't been chosen yet, so that half can't be priced or fitted until we pick them — the inspection can go ahead regardless.

7Medium

Dark water stain on the hardwood floor

Flooring / refinishing

Roughly circular dark stain on the oak floor where slime was left sitting. Water has gone through the finish into the timber and reacted with the tannin, so it is in the wood rather than on it. Present for over a week, so it is fully dry — this is a settled stain, not surface residue. The pale flecks in the photo are from attempting to scrape it off. Likely needs oxalic acid (wood bleach) or a spot sand and refinish, with blending to the surrounding boards.

10Medium

Assemble the storage unit on the new pad

Assembly / general

Build the outdoor storage box once the brick base is down. Blocked by item 9, and also depends on the unit arriving before the handyman does — if it hasn't come, skip this one and keep item 9. Dextrus 230 gallon, roughly 62in long x 31in deep x 33in tall, so the pad needs at least that plus room to stand in front with the lid open.

Note from us: Only if the storage unit has actually arrived by the time you're here. If not, just do item 9 and we'll pick this up next visit.
11Medium

Hoses — tighten all connections, untwist the one at the back

Exterior / hardware

All hose connections need tightening so they stop leaking. Separately, the hose at the back is twisted and needs sorting out.

15Medium

Pop the window screen back into the office window

Exterior / hardware

The office window screen is out and needs refitting. It should simply pop back into the frame — likely a few minutes rather than a job in its own right, so worth bundling into the same visit.

16Medium

Run an electrical cable to the deck for an outlet

Electrical

Mount an electricity cable out to the deck so there's a power outlet there. Outdoor-rated outlet and cable, and the run needs to be fixed rather than trailing. Exact position on the deck to be shown on site.
